topic: Sharp regret and post-selection inference for extreme-loss treatment policies under heterogeneous tail indices. MODEL: For each n>=2 and even m>=2 observe n iid records (X,A,L), X uniform on [m], A independent Bernoulli(1/2), with consistency and randomized treatment independent of both potential losses conditional on X. L(a)>=1. The unknown 2m conditional survival functions S_xa are genuine right-continuous survival functions supported on [1,infinity), and for every y>=1 satisfy |S_xa(y)/(c_xa y^(-alpha_xa))-1|<=D y^(-beta), with alpha_xa in [1,4], c_xa in [1/2,1], fixed known beta>0 and D in (0,1/4]. Atoms at 1 are permitted; all asserted generalized quantiles use inf{y:F(y)>=q}. All such laws are included; no common tail index, fixed gaps, or assumed estimator convergence is imposed. Within-person coupling of potential losses is arbitrary. Let Pi_m={pi:[m]->{0,1}:sum_x pi(x)<=m/2}. For 0<tau<=1/(8n), V_P,tau(pi)=Q_(1-tau){L(pi(X))} and V*_P,tau=min_pi V_P,tau(pi). The loss is logarithmic regret log(V_P,tau(pi)/V*_P,tau)>=0. Define R(n,m,tau)=inf over all measurable randomized learners hat_pi with values in Pi_m of sup over the stated Hall class E_P log(V_P,tau(hat_pi)/V*_P,tau). The full record is available to every learner; p_x and propensity are known to everyone. Study all joint sequences n tending to infinity, even m=m_n>=2 and 0<tau_n<=1/(8n), without pre-assuming vanishing regret. beta,D are fixed known constants. Quantiles are finite and positive under the two-sided polynomial tail envelopes. KERNEL: Determine R(n,m,tau) up to constants depending only on beta,D, including unavoidable logarithmic factors and the exact joint-sequence criterion for R tending to zero. Construct a computable capacity-constrained learner attaining the frontier and a same-Hall-class all-measurable-learner lower bound in the identified regimes. The theorem must be uniform over heterogeneous tail indices and local-to-tied tail mixtures; it must derive when sparse dominating cells versus many collectively contributing cells determine the learning difficulty. Neither a presumed rate formula nor a nonzero price for policy selection is part of the conjecture. As the inference rung, construct simultaneous confidence intervals for log V_P,tau(pi) over all pi in Pi_m with uniform asymptotic coverage >=.95, an explicit derived width bound, and consequently coverage for the selected policy; determine the regimes where their width vanishes instead of assuming it equals the regret rate. The key problem is the full population mixture under capacity, not per-cell conditional extreme effects. Exact rates, useful tail thresholds, choice of estimation method, local-dominance normalization and any selection/inference penalty are delegated to derivation. Merely establishing a plug-in upper bound, assuming a common tail index, or proving a fixed-tau policy theorem does not complete this kernel. COMPUTATION: Estimate each cell-arm survival tail with a total thresholded Hall-class estimator (threshold and bias correction to be derived). For each y, start with the sum of estimated control survivals and select at most m/2 most negative treatment-minus-control survival differences. This finite sorting step computes min_pi m^-1 sum_x hat_S_x,pi(x)(y). A scalar monotone inversion locates the minimal policy quantile, and the minimizing subset at that threshold returns a policy. Full enumeration over the finite policy class is an allowed fallback. Simultaneous bias-aware cell-tail envelopes propagate through every policy mixture and generalized quantile inversion without preclassifying dominant cells. Downstream derivation must prove validity, risk, and width uniformly from the raw sample. CONSUMER: Osama, Zachariah and Stoica, Learning Robust Decision Policies from Observational Data (NeurIPS 2020), equation (4), explicitly targets minimization of the marginal upper cost quantile under an unconfounded policy model, and supplies a published implementation (linked in its Section 4). Its finite-sample conformal approach can return an uninformative maximum-cost limit when information is inadequate; for unbounded cost this leaves extrapolated rare-loss choices uncertified. The proposed theorem would give this tail-cost policy workflow a model-based heavy-tail extrapolation rule and an explicit sample-size/covariate-complexity boundary for when choosing among capacity-limited policies is statistically justified. This is the same marginal loss-quantile decision object. No claim is made that the paper's bounded blood-pressure simulation or IHDP score empirically obeys a Hall tail. Xia-Zhang-Kong's ACTG175 analysis is a secondary example of quantile-oriented treatment choice, not evidence for heavy tails. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A paired-cell Hall splice leaves survival equal to (3/4)y^-4 through a threshold T and changes it above T to (3/4)T^-delta y^-(4-delta), with delta=d T^-beta. The draft checks its original-class envelope and likelihood distance. If H heavy controls are missed, exact logarithmic regret h obeys 4h=log(1+(H/m)(exp(delta(b+h))-1)), where b is the oracle log quantile minus log T. This supports a two-cell rate spine proportional to log(1/tau)n^(-beta/(2beta+4)) and separated general bounds, subject to the listed count and testing proof gaps. Checks cover atoms, empty cells, arbitrarily distant extrapolation, local index ties, and population-mass-dependent dominance. Equal mean mistake counts can give different expected regret. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove matching bounds for the distribution of missed heavy cells under unrestricted capacity reallocation and show the hardest configurations cover the full heterogeneous Hall class; derive confidence widths separately. EARLY KILL TEST: Solve the paired-splice product-prior experiment from constant to log(m) testing information with exact expected log loss. Reject any proposed rare-error rate defeated by a capacity strategy; pivot if known generic machinery already supplies the full frontier. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_extreme_policy_tail_mixture_frontier.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published policy-learning results cover regular mean welfare or fixed, non-extreme quantiles, while existing EVT treatment-effect work estimates fixed counterfactual contrasts rather than optimizing the inverse of a selected population survival mixture. Prior CausalSmith constructions separately handle a scalar nonsmooth optimum through sparse/dense moment matching and policy regret through two-point welfare separation. Neither proof survives capacity reallocation: cell-arm sample sizes may be zero, locally tied indices change which cells dominate, and missed heavy cells interact nonadditively after mixture formation and generalized-quantile inversion. A matching converse must control the distribution of missed heavy cells and exact expected log loss after optimal reallocation, rather than only Hamming error, average mistakes, or scalar functional separation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample two-sided characterization of R(n,m,tau) up to beta,D-dependent constants and unavoidable logarithms, with an explicit sorting-and-inversion learner, a same-Hall-class all-measurable lower bound, and an if-and-only-if joint-sequence criterion for vanishing regret.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Regular welfare analyses price policy complexity through VC-type or Gaussian-supremum terms. Here the survival objective at a fixed threshold is additive across cells and the capacity optimum is obtained by sorting m treatment-minus-control survival differences, so enumeration of all binomial(m,m/2) policies may severely overstate complexity. Conversely, rare Hall-splice errors can accumulate nonlinearly after quantile inversion, and unrestricted reallocation can repair some missed-heavy-cell decisions. The missing lower-bound step is an exact product-prior or packing calculation for expected logarithmic loss after optimal capacity reallocation, rather than a Hamming-loss reduction or policywise union bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching upper-and-lower expression for the selection component of regret as a function of m, tau, and effective tail information, with a regime theorem deciding whether log m, log binomial(m,m/2), another effective-dimension factor, or no additional selection penalty is unavoidable.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Honest EVT intervals currently cover one tail or a modest collection of tail levels and treatment contrasts, while winner and policy-confidence methods begin with regular approximately Gaussian value estimators. Prior CausalSmith work likewise treats either bounded finite-action optimal values or one nonregular threshold target and explicitly excludes simultaneous bands. An extreme policy-mixture quantile instead combines Hall bias amplified by log(1/tau), random effective tail counts, changing dominant cells, and generalized inversion without a uniform density lower bound. The proof must exploit the top-k survival-difference representation to avoid a spurious exponential policy-class penalty while still controlling selection and local ties.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A simultaneous confidence family over all policies with uniform Hall-class coverage at least 0.95+o(1), explicit matching upper and lower bounds for maximal width, an if-and-only-if width-vanishing regime, and automatic coverage of any policy selected from the same data.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Average-tail EVT treats predetermined heterogeneous arrays, and heavy-impurity theory shows that shrinking mixture weights generate phase transitions, but neither is uniform over a data-selected family of policy mixtures. A capacity policy changes the chosen arm within each population cell; when alpha_j-alpha_min is of order 1/log(1/tau), neither a single-heaviest-cell approximation nor common-index pooling is uniformly valid. The deterministic tail-equivalence step must be replaced by a local-dominance normalization retaining every cell whose population weight times exp[-(alpha_j-alpha_min) log Q] remains nonnegligible.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform characterization of each policy-mixture log quantile through an explicit effective-dominance functional, with necessary-and-sufficient regimes for one-cell, sparse-cell, and collective contribution and counterexamples covering the local-to-tied boundaries.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing threshold-selection and concentration results begin with one iid heavy-tail sample, while pooling theory presumes usable tail summaries from each component. In the randomized discrete-cell experiment, 2m multinomial counts can be zero, heterogeneous alpha values rule out indiscriminate pooling, and a coordinatewise selector can accumulate an artificial log m penalty or invalidate the selected policy jointly. Although beta and D are fixed and known here, the usable threshold still depends on unknown cell-arm tail behavior and random occupancy. The first proof step must replace a one-sample order-statistic bound at deterministic k with a simultaneous random-count inequality containing an explicit no-information branch, then show stability under top-k sorting and generalized-quantile inversion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit total cell-arm threshold and bias-correction rule with simultaneous finite-sample Hall survival envelopes, a matching minimax log-error bound under multinomial counts, and a theorem that the induced policy-mixture quantile bounds attain the optimal joint n,m,tau rate.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames threshold choice as a concrete bias-variance problem and connects a computable selector to a nonasymptotic oracle inequality.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Extreme extrapolation depends on how many upper order statistics are retained -> fixed thresholds cannot balance approximation bias and stochastic error -> concentration and Lepski selection yield a total rule for one sample -> policy mixtures require a simultaneous random-cell rule that remains valid with empty cells

method_exemplars.technique: Use quantile transforms and the Renyi representation to obtain Hill concentration, then apply multiscale Lepski threshold selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the natural cellwise ingredients, but they must be simultaneous over random counts and strengthened to survival-level Hall envelopes.

method_exemplars.technique: Incorporate an explicit worst-case second-order-bias envelope instead of estimating fragile nuisance parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Known beta and D make bias envelopes natural; the new difficulty is simultaneous cellwise calibration and stable policy-mixture inversion.

method_exemplars.technique: Pool Hill and Weissman statistics using effective-sample-size weights with explicit variance and bias comparisons.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a collective-cell estimator template, while the destination must choose between pooling and dominance without imposing a common tail index.

literature_map:
Hall (1982, JRSSB, DOI:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1982.tb01183.x) and Hall–Welsh (1985, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/aos/1176346596) establish the classical second-order Pareto rate spine.
Carpentier–Kim (2015, Statistica Sinica, arXiv:1309.2585) proves adaptive and minimax tail-index rates; Boucheron–Thomas (2015, EJS, arXiv:1503.05077) adds concentration and Lepski thresholding.
Sasaki–Wang (2024, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2210.05074) shows that honest extreme-quantile confidence intervals must pay for worst-case second-order bias.
Einmahl–He (2023, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/23-AOS2294) makes the average distribution the relevant tail target under heterogeneous sampling.
He–Einmahl (2026, JASA, DOI:10.1080/01621459.2026.2676731) extends average-tail EVT but continues to study predetermined heterogeneous arrays rather than selected policy mixtures.
Daouia–Padoan–Stupfler (2024, Bernoulli, arXiv:2111.03173) develops pooled Hill and Weissman estimators, but common-tail pooling does not cover locally tied unequal indices selected by policy.
Panov–Morozova (2021, Mathematics, arXiv:2103.07689) finds phase transitions in triangular heavy-impurity mixtures, supporting the sparse-versus-collective dominance opportunity.
Chernozhukov–Fernández-Val (2011, ReStud, arXiv:0912.5013) and Zhang (2018, Annals of Statistics, DOI:10.1214/17-AOS1673) provide foundational extremal-quantile inference, not constrained policy learning.
Huang–Li–Peng (2025, JBES, arXiv:2209.00246) gives uniform EVT inference for extreme continuous-treatment effects over tail levels and treatment pairs.
Wang–Zhou–Song–Sherwood (2018, JASA, DOI:10.1080/01621459.2017.1330204) studies the same marginal policy-outcome quantile at fixed levels.
Osama–Zachariah–Stoica (2020, NeurIPS, arXiv:2006.02355) supplies the closest upper-cost policy motivation, but its conformal certificate can become the outcome-support maximum.
Kitagawa–Tetenov (2018, Econometrica, DOI:10.3982/ECTA13288) and Athey–Wager (2021, Econometrica, arXiv:1702.02896) deliver sharp constrained mean-welfare regret machinery, not beyond-sample quantile regret.
Cui–Han (2026, JASA, arXiv:2311.15878) studies quantiles of individual treatment effects, a different object requiring the joint potential-outcome law.
Andrews–Kitagawa–McCloskey (2024, QJE, DOI:10.1093/qje/qjad043) establishes winner's-curse corrections after treatment selection.
Chernozhukov–Lee–Rosen–Sun (2025, arXiv:2502.10653) gives confidence-aware policy selection for regular Gaussian value estimates; the bias-aware extreme-policy analogue remains open.
